findings.title: deleteMany `retryCount > 1` arm is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany()` call matches `retryCount > 1` for *every* row in `WorkflowReminder`, with no `method` filter. This SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders too as soon as anything starts incrementing `retryCount` for them (e.g. when the same retry logic is added to `scheduleEmailReminders`/`scheduleWhatsappReminders`, or if a future writer sets the field). It also deletes rows that are already `scheduled: true` with a `referenceId`, losing the record needed to cancel the scheduled message later. The branch should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and arguably `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: retryCount update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update()` added at the top of the `catch` block is not itself protected. Before this change the catch only called `console.log`, so any error for one reminder was swallowed and the loop continued. Now, if this update throws (row deleted concurrently by the `deleteMany` of a parallel invocation → Prisma P2025 "record not found", or a DB connection error, which is exactly the kind of failure likely to have caused the original exception), the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop, every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the expected response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`) so a bookkeeping failure cannot abort the batch.

findings.title: Transient failures cause permanent deletion of pending SMS reminders
findings.body: `retryCount` is incremented for every failure path without distinguishing permanent errors (invalid phone number, which is the motivating case) from transient ones (Twilio outage/5xx, network timeout, DB hiccup, rate limiting). Since the cron processes all reminders due within the next 7 days on every run, two consecutive bad runs are enough to push `retryCount` to 2 for the entire backlog, and the next run's `deleteMany` silently deletes all of them — reminders that would have sent fine are lost permanently with no notification. Consider only counting non-retryable Twilio errors, or using a time-based backoff/last-attempt timestamp so retries are spread out rather than consumed within minutes/hours of each other.

findings.title: No retry accounting when message is empty or sendTo is missing
findings.body: The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` not set for an SMS_ATTENDEE step) or the rendered `message` is empty, the loop body falls through without touching the row: `scheduled` stays `false` and `retryCount` stays unchanged, so this reminder is re-selected and re-processed (including the `prisma.profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl` queries) on every cron invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. That is precisely the endless-rescheduling behaviour this PR is meant to eliminate, and it remains unfixed for these cases.

findings.title: OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run
findings.body: The rewritten `deleteMany` produces `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. There is no index on `retryCount` (the schema only has `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` and `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`), so the OR prevents an index-only plan and Postgres will sequentially scan the whole `WorkflowReminder` table each time this cron runs. On a table of this size (one row per reminder per booking) that is a noticeable repeated cost. Splitting into two `deleteMany` calls (one per condition, with the retry one scoped to `method: SMS`) and/or indexing the retry predicate would keep the existing index usable.

findings.title: Comment no longer describes what the delete query does
findings.body: The comment `//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date` now sits above a query that also deletes any reminder (of any method) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. A reader relying on the comment will not realise rows are being removed for retry exhaustion, which is the main new behaviour here. Update the comment to mention the retry-count deletion.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
findings.body: The PR introduces behaviour that permanently deletes user-facing reminders (increment on failure, delete when `retryCount > 1`) and no test covers it: there is no assertion that a failed `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, that a falsy (non-throwing) return also increments it, that a successful schedule leaves the row intact, or that the delete threshold yields exactly two attempts. Given the data-loss consequence of an off-by-one here (threshold `gt: 1` vs `gte: 1`), a unit test around the handler with a mocked twilio provider would be worth adding.
